summary: Silverline Health private deployment: intermittent connection flaps causing 5xx and session resets (major incident escalation)
description:
Issue summary:
Silverline Health (private deployment in prod-us-east) experienced intermittent connection flaps beginning 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC that resulted in 5xx responses and session resets for streaming and non-streaming requests. Errors observed by customer were TLS handshake failures and abrupt HTTP/2 stream resets. This ticket documents the escalation, short-term mitigation, and post-incident follow-up actions.

Impact:
- Customer-facing production traffic experienced ~12% error rate during peak window (08:12–10:03 UTC).
- Streaming sessions dropped mid-response; several business-critical flows retried and saw increased latency.
- Customer single-tenant private control plane hosting their dedicated gateway was affected; no hosted tenants impacted.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC: Silverline CS reports increased 5xx and streaming disconnects via support@ and opens escalation.
- 2026-03-10 08:28 UTC: Triage call with SRE, Private deployment ops, and Silverline network engineer.
- 2026-03-10 08:45 UTC: SRE identifies bursts of TCP connection churn and TLS handshake errors on control-plane VMs.
- 2026-03-10 09:10 UTC: Short-term mitigation applied: increased NLB idle-timeout from 60s -> 300s and temporarily disabled TLS session resumption on control-plane proxy to prevent stale cache reuse.
- 2026-03-10 09:35 UTC: Error rate falls to <1%; customer confirms nominal traffic and accepts workaround.
- 2026-03-11–2026-03-12: Root cause investigation and repro in staging cluster.
- 2026-03-12 17:00 UTC: Deploy permanent control-plane patch rolling TLS session cache eviction fix and bumped connection pool thresholds.
- 2026-03-13 10:00 UTC: Customer acceptance testing complete; ticket moved to Resolved.

Steps to reproduce (internal notes):
1) On a private control plane with NLB configured to default idle timeout (60s), run a bursty client that opens many short-lived connections and reuses TLS sessions.
2) Observe TLS handshake failures and occasional HTTP/2 RST_STREAM when the control-plane proxy's session cache evicts entries under memory pressure.
3) Reproduce was easier when a scheduled batch job from customer peaked at 08:00–08:20 UTC, causing ephemeral connection churn.

Logs / Artifacts / Dashboards:
- Control-plane proxy logs: tls: handshake error: local error: tls: bad record MAC (sampled at 2026-03-10T08:40Z).
- NLB metrics: connection_count spikes and increased connection resets (link to dashboard).
- Packet capture (sanitized) shows client attempting session resumption followed by full handshake failures.
- Customer-provided application logs indicating retries and increased end-to-end latency.

Initial mitigation and communications:
- Applied NLB idle-timeout increase and disabled TLS session resumption temporarily on control-plane proxies; documented change and timeline to customer.
- Proactively opened a dedicated Slack channel (#support-silverline-private) for live updates and arranged an executive escalation bridge for the first 2 hours.
- CS notified customer of potential brief restarts during patch rollout; provided rollback plan.

Root cause hypothesis: 
- Combination of (a) control-plane proxy TLS session cache evictions under memory pressure and (b) aggressive upstream client connection churn (customer batch job) caused increased TLS full handshakes and transient handshake failures. The problem was amplified by a low NLB idle timeout which led to more frequent connection reestablishment and pressure on the proxy session cache.

Resolution summary:
- Short-term: increased NLB idle timeout and disabled session resumption to avoid stale cache lookups; temporarily increased control-plane proxy memory limits to reduce evictions.
- Long-term: patch to TLS session cache logic that avoids returning partially-evicted entries, connection pool tuning, and an infra automation change to detect sudden connection churn and automatically raise NLB timeout for private deployments.

Post-incident follow-up items (see remediation_actions):
- Coordinate a runbook update for private-control-plane networking and TLS settings.
- Validate similar private deployments for the same signal and schedule proactive configuration changes for high-burst customers.

Attachments: links to logs, packet captures, and the root-cause analysis doc archived in Confluence.

resolution_notes: Control-plane TLS session cache bug fixed and deployed; NLB idle timeout increased; proxy memory and connection pools tuned. Customer validated fix during acceptance testing. Runbook updated and scheduled automation for detecting connection churn drafted. No further recurrence in 72-hour observation window.
root_cause_summary: A race in the control-plane TLS session cache caused partially-evicted entries to be returned during high churn; combined with a low NLB idle timeout and customer-side bursty connection patterns this produced handshake failures and stream resets.
remediation_actions: short_term_workaround: Increase NLB idle timeout to 300s and disable TLS session resumption on affected proxies.
medium_term_fix: Patch TLS session cache to only return fully-valid entries and increase proxy memory limits and connection pool thresholds.
long_term_action: Add infra automation to detect abrupt connection churn signals and auto-tune NLB/timeout settings for private deployments; add health-check webhook for customer request.
runbook_update: Update private-control-plane runbook to include detection queries and escalation checklist used during this incident.
